prerequisites: Basic knowledge in physics, computer science and mathematics

learning_outcomes.text: Gaining knowledge in the field of: basic laws of electrical engineering, electronic components and their characteristics, and electronic signal processing.
Acquisition of the ability to use the basic laws of electrical engineering in the calculation of electrical circuits and to recognize and analyze simple electronic circuits.
Is ready to supplement and critically evaluate specialist knowledge and is able to select appropriate sources of knowledge and learning methods

syllabus_topics: Branch circuits analysis with the Kirchhoff’s Current and Voltage Laws
Definition and examples of linear and nonlinear circuit elements
Electronic systems: voltage and current stabilizers
Types of flip-flops: SR, D, JK, and T flip-flops
Study of DC circuits containing linear and nonlinear elements
R, L, and C elements in sinusoidal AC circuits
Measurement of power and energy in single-phase systems
Rectifier diodes - rectifier circuits and filters
Stabilization diodes - current and voltage stabilizers
teaching_methods: Laboratory classes conducted at the University on the research stands
Students work in groups, performing laboratory exercises

assessment_methods.method: Activity and independence in class (laboratory exercises)

assessment_rules: The condition for passing the course is to achieve all the required learning outcomes. Obtaining positive grades from the laboratory and lecture is tantamount to passing. The final grade for the lecture is 100% based on the written test. For laboratory exercises, the condition for credit is to achieve all required learning outcomes and obtain positive grades; the final grade is 40% report, 40% test, and 20% activity and independence in class.
